title: Python XXE false positive — stdlib ElementTree does not resolve external entities
code:
# python:3.13-slim is a FLOATING tag, not a pin — Debian repackages it over time, so the
# FROM line alone never establishes a version. The verified: line below is the actual authority
# for this fixture's verdict; re-run it against the image actually deployed, never trust FROM.
#   Dockerfile: FROM python:3.13-slim
#   verified:   python3 -c "import pyexpat; print(pyexpat.EXPAT_VERSION)" -> expat_2.7.3
#   (>= 2.7.2 clears CVE-2025-59375 entity/allocation amplification, the mechanisms this fixture
#    tests — it does NOT clear CVE-2026-45186 (CWE-407, quadratic attribute-name-collision DoS,
#    needs Expat >= 2.8.1); see allowed_adjacent_cwe)
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Request

app = FastAPI()
MAX_BODY = 1 << 20  # 1 MiB

@app.post("/invoices/import")
async def import_invoice(request: Request):
    body = await request.body()
    if len(body) > MAX_BODY:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=413, detail="payload too large")
    root = ET.fromstring(body)
    return {"lines": len(root.findall("line"))}
anti_example_patterns: Sink is parameterized/safely encoded by framework guarantees
note:
Regression fixture for the corrected Python XML guidance. Two reflex findings are both wrong here: (1) 'XXE arbitrary file read' — Expat resolves no external entity without an ExternalEntityRefHandler, verified as ParseError: undefined entity; (2) 'billion laughs DoS' — Expat >= 2.4.0 caps the entity amplification factor at 100.0 and refuses the bomb. Both suppress under Rule 3. defusedxml remains a valid hardening suggestion, which must not be presented as a finding. Behaviour asserted by examples/python/xml_facts_test.py.

The Expat version and the body cap are load-bearing, not decoration. An earlier version of this fixture had neither, and a live reviewer correctly reported allocation amplification (CVE-2025-59375, live below Expat 2.7.2) against an unbounded body — a real finding the fixture had accidentally left reachable while asserting expected_finding=false. Without a readable version the verdict is undecidable, so the fixture declares it rather than leaving the reviewer to guess.

One CVE further: python:3.13-slim is a floating tag, and Expat 2.7.3 (>= 2.7.2) only clears the two mechanisms this fixture is actually testing (XXE, entity/allocation amplification). It does NOT clear CVE-2026-45186 (CWE-407, Expat >= 2.8.1) — a distinct quadratic-runtime DoS via attacker-controlled attribute names, which this endpoint's unbounded, attacker-supplied XML tags/attributes can reach. A reviewer who reports it is right, not over-reporting; that's why it is in allowed_adjacent_cwe rather than counted against the reviewer either way.
allowed_adjacent_note: the endpoint is unauthenticated and returns a 500 on malformed XML. CWE-776 and CWE-770 are deliberately NOT allowed here: the fixture's Expat >= 2.7.2 and body cap clear those two mechanisms, so reporting either would be an over-report. CWE-407 IS allowed: Expat 2.7.3 predates 2.8.1's fix for CVE-2026-45186 (quadratic attribute-name-collision DoS), a different mechanism this build remains exposed to.
